title: Blood pressure on standing up
summary: Arterial blood pressure and the ECG as a healthy volunteer stands up.
description: Blood pressure was measured beat by beat at a finger, with an ECG, while a healthy volunteer lay on a tilt table and then stood up. On standing, blood pools in the veins of the legs: venous return, stroke volume and arterial pressure fall within seconds. The baroreceptor reflex then speeds the heart and constricts blood vessels, and the pressure recovers. Switch on the heart-rate channel to follow the heart rate.
look_for: The systolic and diastolic pressures before standing up
The fall in pressure in the first seconds after standing, and how long it takes to recover
The heart rate before and after standing up

channels.name: Blood pressure (finger)
channels.about: the arterial pressure at a finger, measured continuously by a cuff that follows it

beats.note: The beats were found automatically by the workbench (the R waves of ECG), and checked by eye, but not by a cardiologist.

subject.notes: A healthy volunteer (180 cm tall, 100 kg), as the database records.
